t.E530.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for magnesium oxide as 'not limited'; the evaluation stated that no toxicological reason was seen to limit use in line with good manufacturing practice, but that the total magnesium intake from these additives should be kept in mind from a nutritional point of view. In the EU it is a Group I additive; EFSA's re-evaluation has not yet been published (it was included in a call for data in 2016).
t.E530.body: Like magnesium in food, the magnesium it contains is absorbed in the last part of the small intestine; at usual intakes generally 40–50% is absorbed, and the proportion falls as intake rises. The kidneys mainly regulate the amount in the body; unabsorbed magnesium is excreted in the faeces.
t.E530.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E530.prod: It is obtained by burning (calcining) limestone or magnesium minerals.
t.E530.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E530.regx.2: Included in the call for use/concentration data as part of the re-evaluation (deadline 31.01.2017).
t.E530.summary: Magnesium oxide. Used as an anti-caking agent and acidity regulator.
t.E530.what: It is a base used to regulate acidity, to neutralise and to prevent caking. In food it reacts with acids to form magnesium salts.
